issue.title: FFT processing in parallel group on supernova causes loud distortion (macOS)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issues that relate to unexpected/unwanted behavior. Don't use for PRs.

issue.body:
<!-- Please see CONTRIBUTING.md for guidelines. -->

## Environment

* SuperCollider version: 3.10.3
* Operating system: macOS 10.13.6
* Other details (Qt version, audio driver, etc.):

## Steps to reproduce
This was previous reported as issue with PartConv, but actually seems to apply to FFT processing in general on my machine.

```supercollider
(
//CAREFUL! this will create LOUD DISTORTION
~numSynths = 2;

~syncBetweenSynths = true; //works fine
// ~syncBetweenSynths = false; //THIS WILL CREATE LOUD DISTORTION

Server.supernova;

s.waitForBoot {

	SynthDef(\pt_test, {arg playbuf = 0, irbuf = 0, amp = 0.5, out = 0;
		var sig, chain;
		sig = SinOsc.ar(300, 0, amp);
		chain = FFT(LocalBuf(2048), sig);
		sig = IFFT(chain); // inverse FFT
		Out.ar(out, sig * amp);
	}).add;

	~target = ParGroup();
	s.sync;

	~allSynths = ~numSynths.collect({|inc|
		var synth = Synth(\pt_test, [\amp, -26.dbamp, \out, inc], ~target);
		if(~syncBetweenSynths, {s.sync});
		synth;
	});
}
)

//free everything
(
~target.free;
currentEnvironment.clear;
)
```

## Expected vs. actual behavior

<!-- Paste error messages in entirety. Use gist if very long. -->
<!-- If SC crashed, see CONTRIBUTING.md for how to make a crash report. -->
Actual behavior:
When multiple ~~PartConvs~~ synths with FFT are started in a parallel group at the same time, they output loud distortion. If they are started after waiting for the server to allocate resources for the previous Synth, or if it's a regular group, they work fine.

Expected behavior: 
Multiple ~~PartConvs~~ synths with FFT  start simultaneously in a ParGroup without issue.

## Discussion:
It seems to be an issue with the vDSP implementation, as indicated in the [source](https://github.com/supercollider/supercollider/blob/develop/common/SC_fftlib.cpp#L24). Building supernova with the internal `Green FFT` library fixes the problem (although that's arguably not a proper "fix").

comments.body: I wasn't immediately able to reproduce (Ubuntu, 3.10.2-rc1). I'll try this again later today.

Few more observations:

- it does behave the same for me on macOS with 3.10.0ish, 3.10.1, 3.10.2-rc1
- additionally, it occurs also when more than one PartConv is started within a parallel group, _regardless of timing_, if
  - using built-in input/output on the macbook pro
  - not specifying hardware buffer size
- I tested on Ubuntu, and the error indeed did not occur

To clarify the second point - it works (and breaks) as described in the PR, with the exception of using built-in in/out _and_ not specifying hardware buffer size, when it breaks regardless of the  `syncBetweenSynths` flag (outputs loud noise). ~~Maybe there is some kind of weird interaction between memory allocation and the PortAudio backend?~~

Edit: 
I tested this also with supernova built with native JACK backend (on macOS, with jackosx), and it also breaks (regardless of timing). In that case I guess this is not related to the PortAudio backend.

What are the async things that should happen before sync?
I suppose that SynthDef sending only?

@sonoro1234 
Do you mean in the reproducer for the bug?
Then it think the following should happen before the sync:
- ~~sending a synthdef~~ 
- allocating playbuf and partconv buffers
- starting pargroup

But the sync triggered by `~syncBetweenSynths` only waits for sending the synthdef and nothing else as the other async tasks already have a sync afterwards.
It is strange that only synthdef sending causes this!

@dyfer
I could not find sync related actions on PartConv. There is no LOCK_SNDBUF_SHARED which could create problems between threads.
I remember that I did a correction on PartConv https://github.com/supercollider/supercollider/pull/2015
It is a complicated UGen and I did a rework for not needing the preparation phase which I am using in my personal work with supernova and dont show any problem. It is here https://github.com/sonoro1234/DWGReverb/blob/master/PartitionedConvolutionTrig.cpp, snappiz did the sclang part. Perhaps you could give it a try?
The whole repo is https://github.com/sonoro1234/DWGReverb

by the way, I could not find the meaning of `(1, 0.99998 .. 0)` What is it doing?

Could you confirm whether this happens on your machine? (the code in the first post is updated accordingly)

> by the way, I could not find the meaning of (1, 0.99998 .. 0) What is it doing?

This is another way of creating arithmetic series. Syntax is a little different than `Array.series` - it is `(first, second .. last)`.
```SuperCollider

-> [ 1.0, 0.99998, 0.99996, 0.99994, 0.99992, 0.9999, 0.99988, 0.99986, 0.99984, 0.99982, 0.9998, 0.99978, 0.99976, 0.99974, 0.99972, 0.9997, 0.99968, 0.99966, 0.99964, 0.99962, 0.9996, 0.99958, 0.99956, 0.99954, 0.99952, 0.9995, 0.99948, 0.99946, 0.99944, 0.99942, 0.9994, 0.99938, 0.99936, 0.99934, 0.99932, 0.9993, 0.99928, 0.99926, 0.99924, 0.99922, 0.9992, 0.99918, 0.99916, 0.99914, 0.99912, 0.9991, 0.99908, 0.99906, 0.99904, 0.99902, 0.999, 0.99898, 0.99896, 0.99894, 0.99892, 0.9989, 0.99888, 0.99886, 0.99...etc...

(1, 0.99998 .. 0).size;
-> 50000
```

I thought `SC_FFT_VDSP` it active on macOS, while `SC_FFT_GREEN` isn't, right?

When I set the breakpoint in line 198, it halted supernova on boot.

To confirm: I forced building without vDSP, but with the internal `FFT_GREEN` library and the problem **did go away**.

IMO this, combined with inability to reproduce this on linux and windows, does indicate that the problem is with how we use vDSP, likely with the global `SplitBuf` mentioned earlier. I'm all ears for what possible solutions to this would be...

Yes, as the title and tags indicate, this is only with supernova. However, any possible future multithreaded implementation is likely to have this problem if it uses vDSP, as indicated in the [comment in the source](https://github.com/supercollider/supercollider/blob/develop/common/SC_fftlib.cpp#L24).

> Green, then FFTW then vDSP was used on OS X. yes - vDSP provided performance improvements and quality ones as well. We should still use this in scsynth unless you uncover any issues (in my opinion).

Others can chime in, but I would rather not lose vDSP on scsynth, and I am not sure what would be needed to fix vDSP on supernova.
